problems.subject: SAE Management - DNLI-001 - Site 203 - Pt 203-005 - Hospitalization (Fall)
problems.summary: Manage Serious Adverse Event for participant 203-005 at Site 203 who was hospitalized following a fall at home. PI assessed causality as 'possibly related' due to dizziness episode prior to fall. Task includes: review of submitted SAE form and hospital documentation, sponsor causality assessment, coordination with Medical Monitor, collection of additional source documents, regulatory reporting within timelines, and ongoing follow-up until event resolution.

todos.description: Review submitted SAE form (DNLI-001_SAE_Form_203-005_Fall.pdf) and initial hospital admission summary for completeness and accuracy within 24-hour reporting window
Coordinate with Medical Monitor (Sarah Chen) to conduct sponsor causality assessment for the fall/hospitalization event, considering PI's 'possibly related' assessment due to pre-fall dizziness
Request and collect complete hospital discharge summary, diagnostic test results, and all source documentation from Site 203 for the hospitalization event
Submit regulatory SAE reports to applicable health authorities (FDA, EMA, etc.) within required timelines per protocol and regional requirements
Notify IRB/IEC of the SAE per institutional requirements and protocol, including PI and sponsor causality assessments
Provide guidance to Site 203 on follow-up requirements, including frequency of participant monitoring, documentation needs, and resolution criteria
Schedule and conduct follow-up communications with Site 203 to track participant recovery status, obtain updates on hospitalization outcome, and collect resolution documentation
Review dizziness as potential safety signal - query if other participants in Part B have reported similar symptoms and consider need for protocol safety amendment or DSMB notification
Document all SAE management activities, decisions, and communications in the Trial Master File and study tracking systems
Upon event resolution, obtain final hospital discharge summary and close out SAE case with final causality assessment and outcome documentation

threads.name: URGENT: SAE Report - Study DNLI-001 - Site 203 - Participant 203-005
threads.description: An urgent email thread initiated by the Principal Investigator at Site 203 reporting a Serious Adverse Event (SAE). A participant in Part B of the study was hospitalized due to a fall. The thread includes your immediate follow-up questions regarding the event's causality and a request for the completed SAE form and source documentation.

messages.content:
Dear Team,

This is an urgent notification regarding a Serious Adverse Event for participant 203-005 in the DNLI-001 study (Part B).

The participant was hospitalized yesterday evening following a fall at home. They are currently stable and undergoing evaluation.

We are in the process of gathering all necessary source documentation and will forward the completed SAE form as soon as possible, well within the 24-hour reporting window.

Best regards,

Dr. Robert Miller
Principal Investigator
Oakwood Research Center, Site 203

Dear Dr. Miller,

Thank you for the prompt notification. We have received your alert and are on standby.

Please send the completed SAE form and any available source documentation (e.g., hospital admission notes, ER report) as soon as it is available.

We appreciate your diligence.

Best regards,

Maria Garcia
Clinical Research Associate
Synergy Clinical

Hi Maria,

Please find the completed SAE form and the initial hospital admission summary for participant 203-005 attached.

Dr. Miller has assessed the event as 'possibly related' to the investigational product due to the participant reporting a brief episode of dizziness prior to the fall. This is documented in the attached form.

We are awaiting further records from the hospital. Please review and let us know if any immediate additional information is required from our end.

Thank you,

Emily White
Study Coordinator
Oakwood Research Center

Attachments:
- DNLI-001_SAE_Form_203-005_Fall.pdf
- Initial_Hospital_Note_203-005_Redacted.pdf

threads.name: Protocol Deviation - Study DNLI-123 - Site 456 - Subject 101-003 - Missed PK Sample
threads.description: A multi-person email chain involving you, the site's Study Coordinator, and your Clinical Trial Manager regarding a significant protocol deviation. The site self-reported that a participant in the healthy volunteer cohort (Part A) missed their post-dose PK blood draw. The discussion focuses on documenting the deviation and determining the impact on data analysis.

messages.content:
Hi Ben,

I am writing to self-report a protocol deviation for subject 101-003, enrolled in Part A of the DNLI-123 study.

This morning, the participant missed their scheduled 4-hour post-dose PK blood draw. The participant had a family emergency and had to leave the site unexpectedly after the 2-hour draw was completed. All other procedures for the visit were completed as scheduled.

We have documented this event in the subject's source documents and are completing the Protocol Deviation form now. Please advise on any immediate actions required from our side and the next steps for reporting this to the sponsor.

Thank you,

Sarah Chen, CCRP
Study Coordinator
Oakwood Clinical Research Center

Hi Alex and Maria,

Please see the notification below from Site 456 regarding a missed PK sample for a Part A subject. This appears to be a significant deviation given the nature of the healthy volunteer cohort.

Sarah, thank you for the prompt notification. Please send over the completed PD form once it's finalized.

Alex/Maria - Please let us know your thoughts on the potential impact and how you would like us to proceed with documentation and follow-up.

Best regards,

Ben Carter
Clinical Research Associate
Synergy CRO

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@oakwoodcrc.com>

I am writing to self-report a protocol deviation for subject 101-003, enrolled in Part A of the DNLI-123 study.

This morning, the participant missed their scheduled 4-hour post-dose PK blood draw. The participant had a family emergency and had to leave the site unexpectedly after the 2-hour draw was completed. All other procedures for the visit were completed as scheduled.

We have documented this event in the subject's source documents and are completing the Protocol Deviation form now.

All,

Thank you for flagging this. A missed PK sample in the HV cohort is indeed a significant deviation and will require careful assessment.

Alex, please take the lead on this. Can you please follow up with Sarah to ensure the deviation is documented thoroughly in the source and on the PD form? Once you receive the form, please review it and begin drafting an initial impact assessment for our internal clinical pharmacology team. We need to understand how this missing data point affects the overall analysis for this cohort.

Please let me know if you need any support.

Best,

Maria Garcia
Clinical Trial Manager
Denali Therapeutics
